display.text:
# Context Pack: `sprint-execute-resume` — Sprint execute queue and resume Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen, clean tree). Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5. Domain: governed-sprint-delivery. Risk: high. Descriptive only — no defect judgments. ## 1. Purpose Executes the top-level task checkboxes of a validated `plan.md` through a reusable agent session, with product-owned durability around every agent turn: - **Queue execution**: one ordered pass over plan tasks; first turn gets shared sprint context + full queue; later turns are compact continuations in the same session when a reusable session ID exists (fallback: independent full prompts). - **Persist-before-launch checkpointing**: each task is persisted as `running` before the runtime call, and its terminal outcome is persisted before the next task starts; session IDs observed mid-stream are also checkpointed. - **Stop-on-failure discipline**: queue halts on the first failed or cancelled task. - **Stale-running reconcile**: `running` records left by dead owners become `failed` with diagnostics at three distinct points (startup recovery, resume reconciliation, pre-execution check). - **Deferral protocol**: CLI `--defer --reason` (operator) or an agent-authored plan marker `- [/] Task N: ... — Deferred: ` (agent); both require rationale and produce durable `deferred` outcomes; the plan checkbox stays visibly unchecked. - **Resume validation**: `--resume` allows checked/deferred plan markers only when the run state already records matching terminal outcomes per stable task ID. - **Containment**: the agent's working directory is set to the resolved approved target (worktree preferred), with in-prompt safety constraints forbidding git mutation and out-of-scope artifacts. - **Publication**: when every task resolves (complete|deferred), git publication commits the implementation worktree (`All=true`) then the workspace artifacts (`execute.md`, `.run-state.json`), config-gated. Primary code: `internal/sprint/execute.go`, `execute_plan.go`, `execute_state.go`, `execute_target.go`, `execute_model.go`, plus `internal/sprint/publication.go:57-78` and `internal/app/git_publication.go`. ## 2. Entrypoints and control flow ### CLI dispatch (`internal/app/sprint_commands.go:329-368`) - Flag parsing `parseSprintExecuteArgs` (1193-1233): `--task `, `--dry-run|--prompt`, `--resume`, `--defer --reason `, `--model `. Constraints: `--defer` requires `--task`; `--defer` cannot combine with `--dry-run`, `--resume`, or `--model`. Unknown flags → ExitUsage. - Non-dry-run, non-defer runs are wrapped as durable operations: `beginDurableCLICommand(OperationExecuteStart, ...Task: req.TaskID)` (durable_operations.go:49-138 — run-control acceptance, owner claim with lease+fencing, running lifecycle event, heartbeat/cancel-watch goroutine). The command context becomes cancellation-aware. Service is rebuilt via `sprintRuntimeService` (685-711) with the real runtime, publisher (`stagePublisher`: nil publisher when `git.stage_completion=off`), stage runtime models, QA/smoke settings. - Deferral runs `DeferExecuteTask` on the plain (non-runtime) service against `deps.ctx`; no durable wrapper. - Error classification after render: findings present → ExitValidation; error contains "failed tasks" → ExitPartial; contains "runtime" → ExitRuntime; otherwise `mapSprintError`. - Output rendering `renderSprintExecute` (1372-1402): project/sprint, dry-run prompt dump, result message, run-state/summary paths, per-task `id status attempts=N` lines, findings list. Help text at 1530-1531, 1571-1580. ### Web / TUI / flow entrypoints - Web operation spec `"execute"|"execute-start"` maps to `OperationExecuteStatus | OperationExecuteDryRun | OperationExecuteResume | OperationExecuteStart` based on options (`internal/web/operation_handlers.go:646-666`). TUI exposes Execute Status/Dry Run/Start/Resume nav items (`internal/tui/model.go:480-483`). - `internal/app/operation_runner.go:53-58`: execute-start/resume → `service.Execute(ctx, p, s, ExecuteRequest{TaskID, ModelOverride, Resume: kind==OperationExecuteResume})`; dry-run variant at `operations.go:443`. - Flow integration (`internal/sprint/flow.go`): execute is the 8th cumulative stage; `runFlowStage` case StageExecute → `s.Execute(ctx, ..., ExecuteRequest{DryRun: req.DryRun, Resume: true})` (flow.go:241) — flow always resumes. Flow skips its generic planning-stage publication for execute (execute publishes itself, flow.go:142-155, 167) and uses `ExecuteComplete` for the skip check (flow.go:307-308 → verify.go:134-140). ### `Service.Execute` main loop (`internal/sprint/execute.go:129-349`) 1. Acquire mutation lock unless DryRun (`acquireMutationContext`, locks.go:112-126 — cross-process file lease shared by flow/execute/review/smoke/verify; reentrant via context marker). 2. `prepareExecute` (351-384): resolve sprint inputs → `planManifest` → `resolveSprintTarget(create=false)` → read plan artifact → `extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, allowChecked=req.Resume)` → if Resume, `validateResolvedResumeTasks` → TaskID existence check → `executeModelSelection(override)` (override > planning.execute_model > planning.plan_model > runtime provider/model; unresolved model ⇒ finding). Any finding aborts before any write ("execute prerequisites failed validation"). 3. Read planning inputs; `prepareSharedPromptContext(..., persistCache=true)` — code-context-derived shared prefix, cached context pack, fails closed when code-context exists but is invalid (`prompt_context.go:93-123`). 4. DryRun: composes the first (or selected) task's prompt and returns; no state writes, no runtime. 5. Fresh vs resumed state: `records := ExecuteTasksToRecords(tasks, now)`; `state := NewExecuteRunState(sp, target, planPath, PlanFingerprint(mustReadPlan), records, now)`. If `req.Resume` AND load succeeds → `state = reconcileExecuteState(existing, records, now)` (existing records substituted by ID into planned order; stale `running` → `failed` with "recovered stale running task on resume"). Load errors on resume are ignored (fresh state wins). Then unconditional `SaveExecuteRunState`. 6. `executionQueue := executeQueueFromState(state.Tasks, tasks, req.TaskID)` — planned tasks whose record is not complete/deferred, optionally narrowed to one ID. 7. Session reuse gate (186-193): only when `req.Resume` and `state.Target.Path == target.Path`; picks the last filtered record whose Runtime.Model equals the first queued task's effective model and has a SessionID (`reusableExecuteSession`, 563-574). 8. Per-task loop over `state.Tasks` (skips others when TaskID set): - Skip `complete`; `running` → `failed` + "stale-running ... before resume" diagnostic; proceed only if now pending|failed|cancelled. - Mark running, `Attempts++`, StartedAt; persist — failure aborts before launch ("persist running execute task %q"). - Per-task model: inline plan annotation `` overrides batch selection (`executeSelectionForTask`, 739-744). - `continueSession := batchSessionID != "" && models match` → compact `RenderExecuteContinuationPrompt` with empty prefix and `SessionAction="continue"`; otherwise full `renderExecuteSessionPrompt` (RenderExecutePrompt + ordered queue section + direct-input packet: project definition inputs, sprint-index, technical-handbook, reasoning directory inputs, reasoning.md, plan.md). - Metadata: session_mode initial|continue|fresh-fallback, execution_turn, execution_queue_size, model_source, stage, task. - `runtimeRequest` (service.go:1122-1169): scoped runtime store owner/path under the sprint dir, PromptRef with sha256 checksum, trace ID, stable-prefix cache directive. `runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path` (execute.go:245). `OnEvent` wrapper checkpoints any new SessionID into run state under a mutex (save errors captured, surfaced post-run). - `startSprintRuntime` (runtime_metrics.go:116-125): `pruntime.CleanupRuntimeStores(sp.Path, 72h, 2GiB, false)` then `runtime.StartRun`; runtime metrics persisted separately (failure degrades to warning). - Post-run classification precedence (287-313): checkpoint save error → failed/"state-save-failed"; deferral read-back error → failed/"invalid-deferral"; deferral reason non-empty → deferred + rationale diagnostic; ctx cancelled → cancelled; runtime error → failed/"runtime-failed"; ≥1 artifact → complete + evidence entries (paths sanitized by `safeArtifactPath`); warning containing "diagnostic-only" → complete + "diagnostic-only-completion"; else failed/"missing-evidence". - Terminal state persisted ("persist terminal execute task"); checkpoint errors abort the whole command afterwards. Failed or cancelled breaks the loop; single-task mode always breaks. - On success, batchSessionID/batchSessionModel advance from the run result (or task.Runtime fallback). 9. `WriteExecuteSummary` → `projects/

/sprints//execute.md` (plain `os.WriteFile` 0644 inside contained path): counts per status, per-task attempts/evidence/diagnostics lines. 10. Any failed/cancelled ⇒ returns result plus error "execute completed with failed tasks". 11. Best-effort `_ = s.deleteCompletedSessions(...)` per runtime result (deletes session(s)/runtime store; flow.go:26-56). 12. If `allExecuteTasksResolved` (≥1 task, all complete|deferred) → `publishExecuteStage` (publication.go:57-78): implementation publish `{Root: target.Path, All: true}` then workspace publish of `execute.md` + `.run-state.json`; identical commit message "ultraplan: sprint

/ complete execute" with `UltraPlan-Publication:` identity trailer; skipped results filtered when publisher disabled. ### `DeferExecuteTask` (execute.go:29-79) Trims reason; requires non-empty taskID+reason, ≤1000 chars, no `\x00\r\n`. Mutation lock; loads state; rejects deferring complete/deferred tasks; marks deferred (+CompletedAt, "deferred" diagnostic with redacted reason); saves state and summary; unknown ID errors. Does not modify plan.md. ### Resume validation (`validateResolvedResumeTasks`, execute.go:386-421) When resuming and plan.md has `[x]` or `[/]` top-level markers: requires a loadable valid run state ("checked tasks lack execution state" otherwise); each resolved marker must map to matching status (`[x]`→complete, `[/]`→deferred) by task ID; mismatches become blocking findings. ### Target resolution (`ResolveExecuteTarget` / `resolveSprintTarget`, execute_target.go) - Extract `**Target Implementation Directory:**` (bold or plain bullet, backtick-trimmed) from project-index.md; absolute or workspace-root-relative; must stat to an existing directory. - If `.workspace.json` exists it wins (Source ".workspace.json"): validated against current source root (clean-path equality), worktree dir exists and is a dir, same git common dir as source, current branch equals recorded branch. Invalid → findings; unreadable/malformed → findings; absent + create=false → raw source target. - Worktree creation happens at the code-context stage (`create=true` in flow.go:138), not here: `createSprintWorkspace` requires the source be a clean git worktree root (no uncommitted changes), creates `ultraplan//` branch at HEAD under sibling `.basename-ultraplan-worktrees/` dir, writes `.workspace.json` atomically (rollback removes worktree+branch if the record write fails). ### Publication mechanics (`internal/platform/gitpublish/publisher.go`) Modes off|commit|commit-and-push. Resolves repo root + current branch (detached HEAD rejected), acquires `ultraplan-publish.lock` in the git common dir, builds a temporary index (`read-tree parent`, `add -A -- paths`, `write-tree`), skips commit when tree equals parent tree, else `commit-tree -p parent` + `update-ref commit parent` (CAS against concurrent branch movement) + index reconcile. Push honors upstream remote/ref, else pushes HEAD to configured remote with `--set-upstream`; `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, push timeout (default 2m). Path requests are containment-checked against the repo root. ## 3. Inputs / outputs Inputs: - argv flags; workspace root; cwd/env via workspace discovery. - `project-index.md` `Project Scope > Target Implementation Directory` line (agent-writable planning artifact; selects both the agent workdir and the wholesale-commit root). - `plan.md` content: top-level `- [ ] Task N: Name` checkboxes (bold-tolerant), nested `- [ ]` steps, `>` quote lines scanned for `Decision N` / `REQ-N-N` / `AC-N` refs, evidence heuristics (step text containing evidence/verification/test/check), `- [/]` deferral markers with `— Deferred:`/`- Deferred:` suffix reasons, inline `` annotations. Plan must pass `ValidatePlanContent` against the plan manifest first. - Planning inputs packet (requirements/code-context/sprint-index/handbook/reasoning dirs/reasoning.md/plan.md) rendered into the first-turn prompt. - `.run-state.json` or productstate DB record (schemaVersion 1) for resume/status; legacy schemaVersion-0 terminal files recognized read-only. - `.workspace.json` worktree record; config keys (`planning.execute_model`, `planning.plan_model`, `models.primary/default`, `git.stage_completion|remote|push_timeout`, runtime config); live agent runtime. Outputs: - Human stdout render; exit codes (0 ok / 2 usage / validation-class / partial for failed tasks / runtime-class). - Files written: `.run-state.json` (atomic temp+fsync+rename+dir-sync, JSON indent+newline), `execute.md` (plain truncate-write), runtime metrics file, disposable context-pack cache. - Git commits and optional pushes in two repos (implementation worktree, workspace) when all tasks resolved and publishing enabled. - Durable run-control events (accept/claim/lifecycle/heartbeat/terminal) for non-dry-run CLI executions. - Runtime side effects delegated to the agent: file edits inside WorkDir=target.Path, test execution, etc. ## 4. Authoritative state - **`.run-state.json` schemaVersion 1** (`domain.go:12,122-133`): header {schemaVersion, project, sprint, target{path,source}, planPath (contained relative), planFingerprint `sha256:` of whitespace-normalized lowercase plan text, createdAt, updatedAt} + ordered `tasks[]` {id `task-<12 hex>`, identity{name, planLine≥1, decisions[], requirements[], evidence[]}, status, attempts≥0, createdAt, updatedAt, startedAt?, completedAt?, diagnostics[], evidence[], runtime?}. - Statuses: pending / running / complete / deferred / failed / cancelled; terminal = complete|deferred|failed|cancelled (`domain.go:63-70`, execute_state.go:271-273). - **Validation contract** `ValidateExecuteRunState` (execute_state.go:184-268): strict schemaVersion==1; project/sprint identity match; safe contained planPath; fingerprint charset (no `\x00\r\n`); ≥1 task; unique IDs; safe identity text; deferred requires completedAt + a `deferred` diagnostic with non-blank rationale; running requires startedAt; terminal requires completedAt; diagnostics need code+message+time and safe charset; evidence needs kind+summary and optionally a safe relative path. - **Dual-home behavior**: when the productstate DB is enabled, the DB record is authoritative — `Save` writes DB first, then mirrors the file only once every task is terminal (checkpoint semantics, execute_state.go:105-130); `Load` prefers the DB record (state_database.go:38-55). Otherwise the file is primary. Migration hooks exist (`MigrateExecuteStateToDatabase`). - **Legacy compatibility**: schemaVersion-0 `{status: complete|failed|cancelled, files[], testsRun[], blockers[]}` files are historical evidence only (`LegacyTerminalExecuteStatus`), never resumable; `requireCompleteExecute` (verify.go:100-132) additionally accepts that legacy shape (status complete/completed with files[] plus non-empty execute.md) as completion evidence. - **`.workspace.json`** (`execute_target.go:16-27`): {schemaVersion:1, sourceRoot, path, branch, baseline, createdAt}; created at code-context stage; validated on every execute target resolution. - **`execute.md`**: derived human summary; plain WriteFile (not atomic); regenerated after every run/deferral. - **`plan.md`**: user-owned input; execute never writes it. The *agent* may edit markers during a turn; execute re-reads it after each turn (`agentDeferredTaskReason`, 423-450: full manifest + extraction revalidation, returning the marker reason only for the exact task). The recorded `PlanFingerprint` is captured once at state creation (via `mustReadPlan`, which swallows read errors) and is not re-verified later in the loop. - Note (descriptive): a resume attempt with unchecked plan tasks but an unreadable/malformed `.run-state.json` passes prepareExecute (no resolved markers ⇒ no findings; load error ignored at execute.go:177) and proceeds with fresh state, overwriting the prior file on first save. ## 5. Invariants (as implemented) - No runtime launch before the `running` transition is durably saved; no queue advance before the terminal outcome is saved; mid-stream session-ID events are also checkpointed. - Queue stops at the first failed or cancelled task; completed/deferred tasks are never re-executed within a run. - Resume reconciliation matches strictly by deterministic ID (normalized name+decisions+requirements+evidence hash); renamed/edited tasks get new IDs and their old records drop out of the reconciled list; deferral markers and model annotations deliberately do not change IDs (test-asserted). - Stale-running recovery exists in three layers: `ReconcileInterruptedMutation` (startup, code "recovery-interrupted"), `reconcileExecuteState` (resume), and the in-loop pre-execution check ("before resume"). - Deferral requires rationale at every layer: CLI flag validation, plan-marker regex requiring a reason, state-validation rationale diagnostic, and `invalid-deferral` classification when the read-back fails. - Completion gating: success requires ≥1 runtime artifact or an explicit "diagnostic-only" warning; otherwise failed/"missing-evidence". - Agent workdir is exactly the resolved target path (worktree preferred when valid); evidence paths stored in state must be safe relative paths or dropped. - Publication happens only when all tasks are terminal-resolved (complete|deferred); implementation repo commits before workspace artifacts; both silently skipped when publishing is off. - All persisted messages/diagnostics route through redaction/truncation helpers (`safeExecuteText` → `config.RedactValue`, ≤180 chars via `safeError`). - Session reuse additionally requires unchanged target path and equal effective model; otherwise fresh full prompts ("fresh-fallback"). ## 6. Trust boundaries - **plan.md as control input**: checkbox syntax, task names, decision/requirement references, deferral reasons, and `` annotations are parsed from an agent-writable artifact. The annotation string flows into runtime model selection without charset restriction beyond the annotation regex `[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]+`; marker deferral reasons are captured by regex without length limits at parse time (charset-checked later at state validation; redacted at persistence). - **project-index.md** decides which directory the agent may mutate and which repository gets committed wholesale (`All=true`) at publication. - **Agent output → durable state**: artifacts/warnings/session IDs from the runtime become state records; evidence URI must pass `safeRelPath` else stored empty; all free-text redacted. - **Agent constraints are prompt-level** (`ExecuteSafetyInstructions`, execute_target.go:220-227): stay inside approved target; do not create smoke/review/issues artifacts; do not run/request git mutation; no cross-sprint/TUI/hosted work. Technical enforcement of sandbox/permissions belongs to the opencode-agent-runtime surface (configured sandbox/permission policy travels on the runtime request). - **gitpublish** executes git with sanitized env (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, LC_ALL=C), validates remote names (no leading dash, restricted charset), and CAS-updates the branch ref. - **Mutation serialization**: cross-process sprint mutation lease (file lock) plus durable run-control owner fencing serialize execute against flow/review/smoke/verify and other owners. ## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics - Mutates the implementation repo (through the delegated agent), can commit and push it, commits workspace artifacts, deletes completed sessions/runtime stores best-effort, prunes stale runtime stores (>72h, >2GiB). - **Cancellation**: durable-context cancel during a turn classifies the task cancelled (+diagnostic), breaks the queue, persists, returns result with error; run-control finish records cancelled. The in-flight runtime call receives the same ctx. - **Crash/restart**: orphaned `running` records recover to failed on startup reconcile or next resume; cleanup-uncertain marker forces explicit operator handling instead of silent reconcile (locks.go:40-44,101-108); legacy terminal states remain readable. - **Retry**: rerunning without `--resume` rebuilds fresh state (prior file replaced on first save); failed/cancelled/pending tasks restart with Attempts++; `--resume` keeps complete/deferred history and continues the remaining queue, reusing the session when target and model still match. - **Partial failure**: mixed-status state persisted, execute.md reflects counts, command exits ExitPartial-class with "execute completed with failed tasks". - Publication failure after full resolution surfaces as command error while leaving all tasks resolved and state saved (commit may exist without push; push timeout bounded). ## 8. Immediate surface dependencies - **sprint-planning-chain**: `resolveSprintInputs`, `planManifest`, `ValidatePlanContent`, plan artifact reads, direct-input packet composition, shared prompt prefix/context pack. - **sprint-flow-state**: flow dispatches execute (always Resume:true), skips its own publish step for execute, gates skip-checks via `ExecuteComplete`; execute itself does not write flow-state.json. - **opencode-agent-runtime** (`internal/platform/runtime`): Request/Result/Event contract — SessionID/SessionAction continuation, OnEvent stream, Artifacts/Warnings driving completion classification, RuntimeStore scoping/cleanup, usage/metrics summaries. - **repo-publication** (`internal/platform/gitpublish`): policy modes, repo lock, temp-index commit strategy, push semantics. - **product-state-mirror** (`internal/productstate`): authoritative DB record {header, items keyed by task ID with ordinals} behind `ExecuteStateInDatabase`. - **run-control / durable operations**: acceptance, claim, fencing, heartbeats, cancellation watch, terminal proposals wrapping every non-dry-run CLI execute. - **workspace scaffold**: embedded `prompts/execute-sprint.md` documents the superseded agent-authored execution mode (writes legacy schemaVersion-0-style `.run-state.json` itself); still materialisable via `defaults install`. ## 9. Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence) From target-repo `docs/cli-reference.md` (~L306-330, execute section): - One reusable agent session; first turn carries shared context + ordered queue; later tasks are compact continuations; UltraPlan checkpoints each task before advancing; stops on failure/cancellation; writes `.run-state.json` and `execute.md`; requires runtime evidence or a safe diagnostic before marking complete; constrains work to the project-index target; falls back to complete independent prompts when no reusable session ID is supplied. - Deferral: `--task --defer --reason ""` is durable and terminal, shown in execute.md and status counts; plan checkbox remains unchecked; review accepts deferrals only with a matching governed deferred outcome; arbitrary unchecked/manually checked tasks cannot bypass execution; `[/]` marker without `— Deferred: ` is invalid. # Context Pack: `sprint-execute-resume` — Sprint execute queue and resume

Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen, clean tree).
Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5.
Domain: governed-sprint-delivery. Risk: high. Descriptive only — no defect judgments.

## 1. Purpose

Executes the top-level task checkboxes of a validated `plan.md` through a reusable agent session, with product-owned durability around every agent turn:

- **Queue execution**: one ordered pass over plan tasks; first turn gets shared sprint context + full queue; later turns are compact continuations in the same session when a reusable session ID exists (fallback: independent full prompts).
- **Persist-before-launch checkpointing**: each task is persisted as `running` before the runtime call, and its terminal outcome is persisted before the next task starts; session IDs observed mid-stream are also checkpointed.
- **Stop-on-failure discipline**: queue halts on the first failed or cancelled task.
- **Stale-running reconcile**: `running` records left by dead owners become `failed` with diagnostics at three distinct points (startup recovery, resume reconciliation, pre-execution check).
- **Deferral protocol**: CLI `--defer --reason` (operator) or an agent-authored plan marker `- [/] Task N: ... — Deferred: <reason>` (agent); both require rationale and produce durable `deferred` outcomes; the plan checkbox stays visibly unchecked.
- **Resume validation**: `--resume` allows checked/deferred plan markers only when the run state already records matching terminal outcomes per stable task ID.
- **Containment**: the agent's working directory is set to the resolved approved target (worktree preferred), with in-prompt safety constraints forbidding git mutation and out-of-scope artifacts.
- **Publication**: when every task resolves (complete|deferred), git publication commits the implementation worktree (`All=true`) then the workspace artifacts (`execute.md`, `.run-state.json`), config-gated.

Primary code: `internal/sprint/execute.go`, `execute_plan.go`, `execute_state.go`, `execute_target.go`, `execute_model.go`, plus `internal/sprint/publication.go:57-78` and `internal/app/git_publication.go`.

225: 		if continueSession {

227: 			promptPrefix = ""
228: 		} else {
229: 			stagePrompt = s.renderExecuteSessionPrompt(sp, planTask, executionQueue, target, taskSelection)
230: 		}
231: 		composedPrompt, composeErr := composeStagePromptChecked(promptPrefix, stagePrompt)
232: 		if composeErr != nil {
233: 			return result, composeErr
234: 		}
235: 		sessionMode := "initial"
236: 		if continueSession {
237: 			sessionMode = "continue"
238: 		} else if executionTurn > 1 {
239: 			sessionMode = "fresh-fallback"
240: 		}
241: 		runtimeReq := s.runtimeRequest(composedPrompt, map[string]string{
242: 			"project": sp.Project, "sprint": sp.Slug, "stage": string(StageExecute), "task": task.ID, "model_source": taskSelection.Source,
243: 			"execution_session_mode": sessionMode, "execution_turn": fmt.Sprintf("%d", executionTurn), "execution_queue_size": fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(executionQueue)),
244: 		})
245: 		runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path
246: 		if continueSession {
247: 			runtimeReq.SessionID = batchSessionID
248: 			runtimeReq.SessionAction = "continue"
249: 		}
250: 		previousOnEvent := runtimeReq.OnEvent
251: 		var sessionMu sync.Mutex
252: 		var sessionSaveErr error
253: 		runtimeReq.OnEvent = func(event pruntime.Event) {
254: 			if previousOnEvent != nil {
255: 				previousOnEvent(event)
256: 			}
257: 			sessionMu.Lock()
258: 			defer sessionMu.Unlock()
259: 			if event.SessionID == "" || (task.Runtime != nil && task.Runtime.SessionID == event.SessionID) {
260: 				return
261: 			}
262: 			task.Runtime = &ExecuteRuntimeSummary{SessionID: event.SessionID, Model: taskSelection.Model, ModelSource: taskSelection.Source, OmissionReason: "raw runtime payloads omitted"}
263: 			task.UpdatedAt = s.now().UTC()
264: 			state.UpdatedAt = task.UpdatedAt
265: 			if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil && sessionSaveErr == nil {
266: 				sessionSaveErr = err
267: 			}
268: 		}
269: 		run, runErr := s.startSprintRuntime(ctx, sp, StageExecute, runtimeReq)
270: 		sessionMu.Lock()
271: 		checkpointErr := sessionSaveErr
272: 		sessionMu.Unlock()
273: 		result.Runtime = append(result.Runtime, run)
274: 		finish := s.now().UTC()
275: 		task.Runtime = mergeRuntimeSummary(task.Runtime, runtimeSummary(run, taskSelection))
276: 		if runErr == nil {
277: 			batchSessionID = run.SessionID
278: 			batchSessionModel = taskSelection.Model
279: 			if batchSessionID == "" && task.Runtime != nil {
280: 				batchSessionID = task.Runtime.SessionID
281: 			}
282: 		}
283: 		task.UpdatedAt = finish
284: 		task.CompletedAt = &finish
285: 		deferReason, deferErr := s.agentDeferredTaskReason(sp, task.ID)
286: 		switch {
287: 		case checkpointErr != nil:
288: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
289: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "state-save-failed", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.state_save_error", checkpointErr.Error()), At: finish})
290: 		case deferErr != nil:
291: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
292: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "invalid-deferral", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.defer_error", deferErr.Error()), At: finish})
293: 		case deferReason != "":
294: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskDeferred
295: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "deferred", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.defer_reason", deferReason), At: finish})
296: 		case ctx.Err() != nil:
297: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskCancelled
298: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "cancelled", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.cancelled", ctx.Err().Error()), At: finish})
299: 		case runErr != nil:
300: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
301: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "runtime-failed", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.runtime_error", safeError(runErr)), At: finish})
302: 		case len(run.Artifacts) > 0:
303: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskComplete
304: 			for _, artifact := range run.Artifacts {
305: 				task.Evidence = append(task.Evidence, ExecuteEvidence{Kind: artifact.Kind, Summary: safeExecuteText("execute.evidence", firstNonEmptyString(artifact.Description, artifact.ID)), Path: safeArtifactPath(artifact.URI)})
306: 			}
307: 		case hasDiagnosticOnlyCompletion(run):
308: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskComplete
309: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "diagnostic-only-completion", Message: "runtime reported safe diagnostic-only completion", At: finish})
310: 		default:
311: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
312: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "missing-evidence", Message: "runtime succeeded without expected evidence", At: finish})
313: 		}
314: 		if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
315: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("persist terminal execute task %q: %w", task.ID, err)
316: 		}
317: 		if checkpointErr != nil {
318: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("persist runtime session for execute task %q: %w", task.ID, checkpointErr)
319: 		}
320: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskFailed || task.Status == ExecuteTaskCancelled {
321: 			break
322: 		}
323: 		if req.TaskID != "" {
324: 			break
325: 		}
326: 	}
327: 	if err := WriteExecuteSummary(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
328: 		return result, err
329: 	}
330: 	statePath, _ := ExecuteRunStatePath(s.root, sp)
331: 	result.RunStatePath = workspace.Rel(s.root, statePath)
332: 	result.SummaryPath = ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageExecute)
333: 	result.Tasks = state.Tasks
334: 	result.Message = executeResultMessage(state.Tasks)
335: 	if hasFailedExecuteTask(state.Tasks) {
336: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("execute completed with failed tasks")
337: 	}
338: 	for _, run := range result.Runtime {
339: 		_ = s.deleteCompletedSessions(ctx, run)
340: 	}
341: 	if allExecuteTasksResolved(state.Tasks) {
342: 		publications, publishErr := s.publishExecuteStage(ctx, sp, target)
343: 		result.Publications = append(result.Publications, publications...)
344: 		if publishErr != nil {
345: 			return result, publishErr
346: 		}
347: 	}
348: 	return result, nil
349: }

351: func (s Service) prepareExecute(projectRef, sprintRef string, req ExecuteRequest) (Sprint, []ExecutePlanTask, ExecuteTargetRef, ExecuteModelSelection, []ValidationFinding, error) {
352: 	sp, inputs, catalog, err := s.resolveSprintInputs(projectRef, sprintRef)
353: 	if err != nil {
354: 		return Sprint{}, nil, ExecuteTargetRef{}, ExecuteModelSelection{}, nil, err
355: 	}
356: 	manifest, findings := s.planManifest(sp, inputs, catalog)
357: 	var target ExecuteTargetRef
358: 	if len(findings) == 0 {
359: 		var targetFindings []ValidationFinding
360: 		target, targetFindings = s.resolveSprintTarget(sp, inputs.ProjectIndex, false)
361: 		findings = append(findings, targetFindings...)
362: 	}
363: 	var tasks []ExecutePlanTask
364: 	if len(findings) == 0 {
365: 		data, readErr := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StagePlan)
366: 		if readErr != nil {
367: 			findings = append(findings, finding("plan.md", "", ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), "missing plan", readErr.Error(), "Generate and validate plan.md before execute."))
368: 		} else {
369: 			tasks, findings = extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, req.Resume)
370: 			if req.Resume && len(findings) == 0 {
371: 				findings = append(findings, s.validateResolvedResumeTasks(sp, tasks, manifest.OutputPath)...)
372: 			}
373: 		}
374: 	}
375: 	if req.TaskID != "" && len(findings) == 0 && taskByID(tasks, req.TaskID).ID == "" {
376: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", req.TaskID, ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), "unknown execute task", "selected task id does not exist in plan.md", "Use a task id from validate execute or run without --task."))
377: 	}
378: 	selection := s.executeModelSelection(req.ModelOverride)
379: 	if selection.Model == "" {
380: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Configuration", "execute model", "", "missing execute model", "no execute model configured", "Set planning.execute_model, planning.plan_model, models.primary, or models.default."))
381: 	}
382: 	sortSprintFindings(findings)
383: 	return sp, tasks, target, selection, findings, nil
384: }

386: func (s Service) validateResolvedResumeTasks(sp Sprint, tasks []ExecutePlanTask, planPath string) []ValidationFinding {
387: 	var resolved []ExecutePlanTask
388: 	for _, task := range tasks {
389: 		if task.Checked || task.Deferred {
390: 			resolved = append(resolved, task)
391: 		}
392: 	}
393: 	if len(resolved) == 0 {
394: 		return nil
395: 	}
396: 	state, err := LoadExecuteRunState(s.root, sp)
397: 	if err != nil {
398: 		return []ValidationFinding{finding("Tasks", "", planPath, "checked tasks lack execution state", "one or more top-level tasks are checked but no valid resumable execution state exists", "Restore the matching .run-state.json or leave tasks unchecked for a new execution.")}
399: 	}
400: 	byID := make(map[string]ExecuteTaskStatus, len(state.Tasks))
401: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
402: 		byID[task.ID] = task.Status
403: 	}
404: 	var findings []ValidationFinding
405: 	for _, task := range resolved {
406: 		expected := ExecuteTaskComplete
407: 		problem := "checked task is not complete in execution state"
408: 		detail := "top-level task is checked without a matching complete run-state record"
409: 		suggestion := "Restore the task checkbox to unchecked or reconcile the execution state before resuming."
410: 		if task.Deferred {
411: 			expected = ExecuteTaskDeferred
412: 			problem = "plan deferral is not recorded in execution state"
413: 			detail = "top-level task uses [/] without a matching deferred run-state record"
414: 			suggestion = "Resume the owning execute attempt so it can record the deferral, or restore the task marker to unchecked."
415: 		}
416: 		if byID[task.ID] != expected {
417: 			findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", task.Name, planPath, problem, detail, suggestion))
418: 		}
419: 	}
420: 	return findings
421: }

423: func (s Service) agentDeferredTaskReason(sp Sprint, taskID string) (string, error) {
424: 	data, err := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StagePlan)
425: 	if err != nil {
426: 		return "", err
427: 	}
428: 	inputs, err := s.store.ReadPlanningInputs(sp)
429: 	if err != nil {
430: 		return "", err
431: 	}
432: 	catalog, parseFindings := project.ParseProjectIndex(inputs.ProjectIndex)
433: 	if len(parseFindings) > 0 {
434: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("project-index.md has malformed catalog rows")
435: 	}
436: 	manifest, findings := s.planManifest(sp, inputs, catalog)
437: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
438: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("plan manifest is invalid")
439: 	}
440: 	tasks, findings := extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, true)
441: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
442: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("plan changed to an invalid task state")
443: 	}
444: 	for _, task := range tasks {
445: 		if task.ID == taskID && task.Deferred {
446: 			return task.DeferReason, nil
447: 		}
448: 	}
449: 	return "", nil
450: }

620: func reconcileExecuteState(existing ExecuteRunState, planned []ExecuteTaskRecord, now time.Time) ExecuteRunState {
621: 	byID := map[string]ExecuteTaskRecord{}
622: 	for _, task := range existing.Tasks {
623: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskRunning {
624: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
625: 			task.CompletedAt = &now
626: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "stale-running", Message: "recovered stale running task on resume", At: now})
627: 		}
628: 		byID[task.ID] = task
629: 	}
630: 	for i, task := range planned {
631: 		if old, ok := byID[task.ID]; ok {
632: 			planned[i] = old
633: 		}
634: 	}
635: 	existing.Tasks = planned
636: 	existing.UpdatedAt = now
637: 	return existing
638: }

644: func formatRuntimeUsage(usage pruntime.Usage) string {
645: 	var parts []string
646: 	appendKnown := func(name string, known bool, value int64) {
647: 		if known {
648: 			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s=%d", name, value))
649: 		}
650: 	}
651: 	appendKnown("input", usage.InputTokensKnown, usage.InputTokens)
652: 	appendKnown("output", usage.OutputTokensKnown, usage.OutputTokens)
653: 	appendKnown("reasoning", usage.ReasoningTokensKnown, usage.ReasoningTokens)
654: 	appendKnown("cache_read", usage.CacheReadTokensKnown, usage.CacheReadTokens)
655: 	appendKnown("cache_write", usage.CacheWriteTokensKnown, usage.CacheWriteTokens)
656: 	appendKnown("total", usage.TotalTokensKnown, usage.TotalTokens)
657: 	appendKnown("turns", usage.TurnsKnown, usage.Turns)
658: 	return strings.Join(parts, " ")
659: }

60: 		if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "" {
61: 			continue
62: 		}
63: 		if isTopLevelTaskCheckbox(line) {
64: 			flush()
65: 			title, checked, ok, taskModel := parseTopLevelTaskLine(line)
66: 			deferred := isDeferredTaskLine(line)
67: 			deferReason := deferredTaskReason(line)
68: 			if !ok {
69: 				findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", "", manifest.OutputPath, "unsupported task syntax", strings.TrimSpace(line), "Use '- [ ] Task N: Name' or '- [ ] **Task N: Name**'."))
70: 				continue
71: 			}
72: 			if checked {
73: 				if !allowChecked {
74: 					findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", title, manifest.OutputPath, "completed task cannot be executed", "top-level task is already checked", "Leave executable plan tasks unchecked until execute records completion."))
75: 				}
76: 			}
77: 			if deferred {
78: 				if deferReason == "" {
79: 					findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", title, manifest.OutputPath, "deferred task lacks rationale", "top-level task uses [/] without an inline Deferred reason", "Use '- [/] Task N: Name — Deferred: concrete reason'."))
80: 				}
81: 				if !allowChecked {
82: 					findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", title, manifest.OutputPath, "deferred task cannot start a new execution", "top-level task is already marked deferred", "Start with [ ] and let execute record the agent's deferral, or resume the matching run state."))
83: 				}
84: 			}
85: 			current = &ExecutePlanTask{Name: title, PlanLine: baseLine + i + 1, Checked: checked, Deferred: deferred, DeferReason: deferReason, Model: taskModel}
86: 			current.Decisions = append(current.Decisions, extractRefs(title, `Decision\s+\d+`)...)
87: 			current.Requirements = append(current.Requirements, extractRefs(title, `(?:REQ-\d+-\d+|AC-\d+)`)...)
88: 			continue
89: 		}
90: 		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimLeft(line, " \t"), "- [") {
91: 			if current == nil {
92: 				findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", "", manifest.OutputPath, "ambiguous checklist item", strings.TrimSpace(line), "Nested checklist items must appear under an explicit top-level Task entry."))
93: 				continue
94: 			}
95: 			item := strings.TrimSpace(stripCheckbox(line))
96: 			current.Steps = append(current.Steps, item)
97: 			lower := strings.ToLower(item)
98: 			if strings.Contains(lower, "evidence") || strings.Contains(lower, "verification") || strings.Contains(lower, "test") || strings.Contains(lower, "check") {
99: 				current.Evidence = append(current.Evidence, item)
100: 			}
101: 			current.Decisions = append(current.Decisions, extractRefs(item, `Decision\s+\d+`)...)
102: 			current.Requirements = append(current.Requirements, extractRefs(item, `(?:REQ-\d+-\d+|AC-\d+)`)...)
103: 			continue
104: 		}
105: 		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
106: 		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, ">") && current != nil {
107: 			current.Decisions = append(current.Decisions, extractRefs(trimmed, `Decision\s+\d+`)...)
108: 			current.Requirements = append(current.Requirements, extractRefs(trimmed, `(?:REQ-\d+-\d+|AC-\d+)`)...)
109: 		}
110: 	}
111: 	flush()
112: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
113: 		sortSprintFindings(findings)
114: 		return nil, findings
115: 	}
116: 	if len(tasks) == 0 {
117: 		return nil, []ValidationFinding{finding("Tasks", "", manifest.OutputPath, "no executable tasks", "no supported unchecked top-level Task checklist entries were found", "Add explicit '- [ ] Task N: ...' entries.")}
118: 	}
119: 	seen := map[string]ExecutePlanTask{}
120: 	for _, task := range tasks {
121: 		if prior, ok := seen[task.ID]; ok {
122: 			findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", task.Name, manifest.OutputPath, "duplicate task id", fmt.Sprintf("%s duplicates %s", task.Name, prior.Name), "Make task identity fields distinct."))
123: 		}
124: 		seen[task.ID] = task
125: 	}
126: 	sortSprintFindings(findings)
127: 	return tasks, findings
128: }
129: 
130: func PlanFingerprint(content string) string {
131: 	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(normalizeTaskText(content)))
132: 	return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
133: }
134: 
135: func ExecuteTasksToRecords(tasks []ExecutePlanTask, now func() time.Time) []ExecuteTaskRecord {
136: 	records := make([]ExecuteTaskRecord, 0, len(tasks))
137: 	current := now()
138: 	for _, task := range tasks {
139: 		records = append(records, ExecuteTaskRecord{
140: 			ID: task.ID,
141: 			Identity: ExecuteTaskIdentity{
142: 				Name:         task.Name,
143: 				PlanLine:     task.PlanLine,
144: 				Decisions:    task.Decisions,
145: 				Requirements: task.Requirements,
146: 				Evidence:     task.Evidence,
147: 			},
148: 			Status:    ExecuteTaskPending,
149: 			Attempts:  0,
150: 			CreatedAt: current,
151: 			UpdatedAt: current,
152: 		})
153: 	}
154: 	return records
155: }
156: 
157: func deterministicExecuteTaskID(task ExecutePlanTask) string {
158: 	parts := []string{task.Name}
159: 	parts = append(parts, task.Decisions...)
160: 	parts = append(parts, task.Requirements...)
161: 	parts = append(parts, task.Evidence...)
162: 	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(normalizeTaskText(strings.Join(parts, "\n"))))
163: 	return "task-" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])[:12]
164: }

166: // taskModelAnnotationPattern matches an inline per-task runtime model
167: // annotation, e.g. `- [ ] Task 1: Name <!-- model: provider/model -->`.
168: var taskModelAnnotationPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)<!--\s*model:\s*([A-Za-z0-9._~/-]+)\s*-->`)
169: 
170: func parseTopLevelTaskLine(line string) (string, bool, bool, string) {
171: 	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
172: 	checked := strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(trimmed), "- [x]")
173: 	body := strings.TrimSpace(trimmed[5:])
174: 	body, _ = splitDeferredTaskReason(body)
175: 	model := ""
176: 	if match := taskModelAnnotationPattern.FindStringSubmatchIndex(body); match != nil {
177: 		model = strings.TrimSpace(body[match[2]:match[3]])
178: 		body = strings.TrimSpace(body[:match[0]] + body[match[1]:])
179: 	}
180: 	body = strings.Trim(body, "* ")
181: 	if !regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^Task\s+\d+\s*:`).MatchString(body) {
182: 		return "", checked, false, model
183: 	}
184: 	body = strings.TrimSpace(strings.Trim(body, "* "))
185: 	return body, checked, true, model
186: }
187: 
188: func isDeferredTaskLine(line string) bool {
189: 	return strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line)), "- [/]")
190: }
191: 
192: func deferredTaskReason(line string) string {
193: 	_, reason := splitDeferredTaskReason(strings.TrimSpace(line)[5:])
194: 	return reason
195: }
196: 
197: func splitDeferredTaskReason(body string) (string, string) {
198: 	re := regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)\s+(?:—|-)\s+deferred:\s*(.+?)\s*$`)
199: 	match := re.FindStringSubmatchIndex(body)
200: 	if match == nil {
201: 		return body, ""
202: 	}
203: 	return strings.TrimSpace(body[:match[0]]), strings.TrimSpace(body[match[2]:match[3]])
204: }
205: 
206: func stripCheckbox(line string) string {
207: 	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
208: 	if len(trimmed) >= 5 && strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "- [") {
209: 		return strings.TrimSpace(trimmed[5:])
210: 	}
211: 	return trimmed
212: }
213: 
214: func extractRefs(text, pattern string) []string {
215: 	re := regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)` + pattern)
216: 	matches := re.FindAllString(text, -1)
217: 	out := make([]string, 0, len(matches))
218: 	for _, match := range matches {
219: 		out = append(out, strings.TrimSpace(match))
220: 	}
221: 	return out
222: }
223: 
224: func sectionStartLine(content, section string) int {
225: 	re := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^#{2,6}\s+` + regexp.QuoteMeta(section) + `\s*$`)
226: 	loc := re.FindStringIndex(content)
227: 	if loc == nil {
228: 		return 0
229: 	}
230: 	return strings.Count(content[:loc[0]], "\n") + 1
231: }
232: 
233: func uniqueSorted(values []string) []string {
234: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
235: 	var out []string
236: 	for _, value := range values {
237: 		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
238: 		if value == "" {
239: 			continue
240: 		}
241: 		key := strings.ToLower(value)
242: 		if seen[key] {
243: 			continue
244: 		}
245: 		seen[key] = true
246: 		out = append(out, value)
247: 	}
248: 	sort.Strings(out)
249: 	return out
250: }
251: 
252: func uniqueStable(values []string) []string {
253: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
254: 	var out []string
255: 	for _, value := range values {
256: 		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
257: 		if value == "" || seen[value] {
258: 			continue
259: 		}
260: 		seen[value] = true
261: 		out = append(out, value)
262: 	}
263: 	return out
264: }

267: 	fields := strings.Fields(strings.ToLower(value))
268: 	return strings.Join(fields, " ")

reasoning_details.text:
Now let me look at the durable operations and the runtime platform Request/Result. Also the `verify.go` ExecuteComplete. Let me check a few key things I've noticed so far as candidate defects:

**Candidate 1: Fresh (non-resume) run overwrites existing run state, losing complete/deferred history.**
At execute.go:174-182: `records := ExecuteTasksToRecords(tasks, now)` — all pending; `state := NewExecuteRunState(...)`. If `req.Resume` is false and an existing state exists, it's discarded. This is documented ("Retry: rerunning without `--resume` rebuilds fresh state"). So this is by design per docs. Not a defect per contract... though there is a subtlety: without `--resume`, if plan.md has checked tasks, extraction fails with findings ("completed task cannot be executed"). OK.

But wait: what about a *fresh* run when plan has no checked markers but state exists? Then prior state file gets replaced with fresh pending records on first save. Documented behavior. Not a defect.

**Candidate 2: Resume with unreadable/malformed run-state silently proceeds fresh.**
execute.go:177: `if existing, loadErr := LoadExecuteRunState(s.root, sp); loadErr == nil && req.Resume { state = reconcileExecuteState(existing, records, now) }`. If loadErr != nil (e.g., malformed JSON), the run proceeds with fresh state and will overwrite the malformed file on first save at line 180. But note `validateResolvedResumeTasks` in prepareExecute: only triggers when plan has checked/deferred markers. If plan is all-unchecked but `.run-state.json` exists and is malformed, resume proceeds fresh and clobbers. Is that a defect? The context pack flags this descriptively. Consider consequences: resume semantics promise "resume validation against plan markers" — with unchecked tasks, there's nothing to validate; starting fresh is arguably correct since no task is marked resolved. But consider partial-progress scenario: run 1 completes tasks 1-2 of 5 (unchecked in plan because execute never checks them!). Hmm wait — does execute ever update plan.md checkboxes? No — "execute never writes plan.md". The agent may edit markers during a turn. So after a successful full run where the agent didn't check any boxes, plan.md remains unchecked, and `.run-state.json` holds all-complete records.

Now suppose `.run-state.json` becomes corrupted (disk issue). Operator runs `execute --resume`: prepareExecute → extractExecutePlanTasks(allowChecked=true) succeeds (no checked markers) → validateResolvedResumeTasks returns nil (no resolved markers) → load fails at line 177 → **fresh state created**, all previously complete tasks re-executed from scratch. That silently discards history and redoes completed work — the exact failure mode that resume exists to prevent ("stale running reconcile", "never redo complete tasks" invariant §5: "Resume reconciliation matches strictly by deterministic ID"). The invariant says "completed/deferred tasks are never re-executed within a run". Across runs via resume, redoing work on a corrupt state file is silent data loss of the completion record. But is it observable bad outcome? Yes: completed tasks are re-run (cost, potential double-mutation), and the previous evidence/attempts history is destroyed (file overwritten). Trigger: corrupt/unreadable .run-state.json + resume + unchecked plan. Counter-evidence: is there any guard? `validateResolvedResumeTasks` only fires for checked/deferred markers. Also note the same happens with ErrExecuteRunStateMissing — which is legitimately fine on first run. But distinguishing missing vs malformed would be easy. Actually wait — let me think about whether ignoring load errors is deliberate. The context pack notes it as descriptive fact #101. Severity: moderate-high reliability. Confidence: real code path. However — is it plausible that a malformed state file exists while plan.md is fully unchecked? The state file could be corrupted by a crash during write (atomic write mitigates), or manual edit, or schemaVersion drift. Also DB-authoritative mode: LoadExecuteRunState prefers DB record; if DB record invalid → error ignored → fresh. Hmm.

Actually, hold on. There's a subtler and more serious variant: **resume when plan.md has NO checked markers and state exists with complete records — normal operation!** In the normal flow, execute never ticks plan boxes (the agent might, but isn't required to). So the typical resume path relies entirely on the run-state file. If the file is missing (deleted by git clean? it's inside the workspace repo... committed actually), or unreadable due to permissions, resume silently starts over. The "load errors on resume are ignored (fresh state wins)" comment in the context pack. Is this intended? For ErrExecuteRunStateMissing, yes — first execution ever with --resume should work. For malformed, arguably not. I'd report as a finding with medium severity: resume silently rebuilds fresh state when the existing run state is malformed/unreadable, destroying prior terminal outcomes and re-executing completed tasks.

Let me verify there's no earlier guard: `validateResolvedResumeTasks` requires checked/deferred markers. Right. And ReconcileInterruptedMutation at startup surfaces malformed state as ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed (locks_test.go mentions). Does CLI call ReconcileInterruptedMutation before execute? Let me check where it's called — maybe web server startup. If the CLI execute path doesn't call it, then malformed state reaches execute.go:177 and is swallowed.

**Candidate 3: `reusableExecuteSession` picks session from a failed/stale task's runtime summary.**
It scans records filtered by req.TaskID, takes the LAST record whose Runtime.Model == model and SessionID != "". It doesn't check status — a failed task's session could be reused. That's arguably fine (continuing a session to retry is reasonable). Not clearly a defect.

More interesting: on resume, `reconcileExecuteState(existing, records, now)` substitutes old records into planned order. Then queue = non-terminal records. batchSessionID = last matching record with model match. Fine.

**Candidate 4: Session checkpoint OnEvent closure captures `task` pointer — loop variable aliasing.** `task := &state.Tasks[i]` — pointer into slice, stable across iterations since indexed. Each iteration defines its own OnEvent. Fine.

But wait — the OnEvent handler saves state while the main goroutine may also be saving (after run completes, OnEvent could fire concurrently with main-loop Save?). After startSprintRuntime returns, events shouldn't fire anymore (unless async). sessionMu protects sessionSaveErr read/write. But `task.Runtime` write inside OnEvent vs main goroutine writing `task.Runtime = mergeRuntimeSummary(...)` at line 275 without holding sessionMu — data race IF events can still arrive after StartRun returns. Depends on runtime contract; likely synchronous. Weak finding.

Also `state.UpdatedAt = task.UpdatedAt` inside OnEvent mutates shared state concurrently with main goroutine reads. Again depends on event delivery being synchronous. The race-guard exists partially (sessionMu only guards sessionSaveErr and serializes OnEvent handlers among themselves). Hmm, actually the mutex suggests the authors considered concurrent events, but main-goroutine accesses aren't synchronized with it. Medium-confidence concurrency nit — need to check runtime implementation whether events can be delivered after return. Let me check internal/platform/runtime.

**Candidate 5: `agentDeferredTaskReason` precedence — deferral check happens BEFORE ctx.Err() and runErr checks.**
Precedence order: checkpointErr > deferErr > deferReason > ctx cancelled > runErr > artifacts. If the agent deferred AND produced artifacts, deferral wins. If context was cancelled mid-turn but agent wrote a deferral marker before cancellation... deferral wins. Plausible design.

Interesting: `deferErr != nil` marks task FAILED even if the runtime succeeded and produced artifacts. E.g., plan.md edited by agent into invalid form mid-turn → whole extraction fails → "plan changed to an invalid task state" → failed. That's the designed containment.

**Candidate 6: Deferral classification when ctx cancelled:** If ctx is cancelled and the agent did NOT write a marker, status=cancelled, break. Good.

**Candidate 7: `hasFailedExecuteTask` includes cancelled → ExitPartial. Fine.

**Candidate 8: Publication gating `allExecuteTasksResolved(state.Tasks)` uses ALL state tasks, but with `req.TaskID` set, only one task ran. So single-task mode can publish everything once the remaining tasks were already resolved in state. That seems right for resume-with---task flows.

BUT notice: publication happens whenever all tasks are complete|deferred — including a **single-task deferral** (`DeferExecuteTask`) — no wait, DeferExecuteTask doesn't publish. Only Execute publishes. But consider: fresh run with TaskID targeting the LAST unresolved task while others are complete in state → publishes. OK.

Now the bigger question: **publication of the implementation repo with All=true commits ANY uncommitted changes in the target worktree**, including changes made outside the sprint (user's own WIP). The agent works in target.Path; user might also have WIP. Publishing `{Root: target.Path, All: true}` stages EVERYTHING. Trust boundary noted in context pack §6. It's config-gated (stage_completion off by default?). Let me check default config. If default is commit-and-push, that's dangerous. Let me check config defaults.

**Candidate 9: `WriteExecuteSummary` plain WriteFile — non-atomic. Crash mid-write leaves truncated execute.md. Publication then commits truncated summary? Publication happens after WriteExecuteSummary success; a crash between write and publish leaves truncated file committed later by another stage? Minor.

**Candidate 10: `DeferExecuteTask` loads state via `LoadExecuteRunState` — in DB-authoritative mode, save mirrors to file only at checkpoint. Defer marks one task deferred; if other tasks still pending, `executeStateCheckpoint` false → file NOT updated but DB updated. Then WriteExecuteSummary(s.root, sp, state) writes summary from in-memory state — consistent with DB. OK-ish. But `Load` prefers DB so subsequent ops consistent.

Hmm wait — actually in DB mode, SaveExecuteRunState writes DB first, then only writes file at checkpoint. But `DeferExecuteTask` then calls `WriteExecuteSummary` unconditionally. Fine.

If process crashes mid-run, recovery via `ReconcileInterruptedMutation` calls `LoadExecuteRunState` which prefers DB — good. But legacy readers reading the FILE see stale state. Acceptable.

Interesting — DB-mirror mode details:

**Candidate A (DB mode + file mirror divergence)**: `ExecuteStateInDatabase(root, s)` returns whether a `sprint_execute` record EXISTS in the DB. In `Save`: if DB record exists → write DB; only mirror to file once ALL tasks terminal. So in DB-authoritative mode with partial progress, the FILE becomes stale (holds whatever was last mirrored — possibly an old checkpoint or nothing).

Now consider: `Load` prefers DB when record exists. Consistent.

BUT what happens on **resume after all tasks became terminal once** (file mirrored), then operator re-runs execute without --resume? Fresh state saved: Save → ExecuteStateInDatabase true → saveExecuteStateDatabase(fresh pending) → not checkpoint → file NOT updated. File still holds OLD complete state while DB holds fresh pending. Then crash before any task completes. Recovery: Load prefers DB → fresh pending. Consistent. OK.

What about **productstate.Existing vs Ensure**: Save uses Ensure (creates DB). Load/Has use Existing. Fine.

**Candidate B — `saveExecuteStateDatabase` mutates shared `state.UpdatedAt`** — fine.

655: 		RunID:             string(event.RunID),

670: // promoteObservablePayloadFields lifts nested runtime facts (tool names, titles,
671: // text deltas, statuses) to the payload top level so downstream consumers —
672: // run-loop progress summaries, durable run journals, and the web timeline — can
673: // read them without depending on adapter-specific nesting. Existing top-level
674: // values always win.
675: func promoteObservablePayloadFields(payload map[string]any) {
676: 	if len(payload) == 0 {
677: 		return
678: 	}
679: 	for _, key := range []string{"tool", "name", "title", "detail", "text", "delta", "output", "message", "state", "status", "action", "phase"} {

681: 			continue
682: 		}
683: 		if found := findNestedPayloadString(payload, key, 0); found != "" {
684: 			payload[key] = found
685: 		}
686: 	}

689: func findNestedPayloadString(value any, want string, depth int) string {
690: 	if depth > 4 {
691: 		return ""
692: 	}
693: 	switch typed := value.(type) {
694: 	case map[string]any:
695: 		if s, ok := typed[want].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(s) != "" {
696: 			return s
697: 		}
698: 		// Deterministic traversal for stable results across map orders.
699: 		keys := make([]string, 0, len(typed))
700: 		for k := range typed {
701: 			keys = append(keys, k)
702: 		}
703: 		sort.Strings(keys)
704: 		for _, k := range keys {
705: 			if found := findNestedPayloadString(typed[k], want, depth+1); found != "" {
706: 				return found
707: 			}
708: 		}
709: 	case []any:
710: 		for _, item := range typed {
711: 			if found := findNestedPayloadString(item, want, depth+1); found != "" {
712: 				return found
713: 			}
714: 		}
715: 	}
716: 	return ""

752: func mapError(err error) error {

755: 	}

767: 		case errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
768: 			bounded.Cause = context.DeadlineExceeded

773: 	}

reasoning_details.text:
Very important findings from runtime.go:

**Finding candidate R1 — OnEvent goroutine race with post-run main-loop state mutation.**
The event pump runs in a separate goroutine (`go func() { for event := range run.Events() { ... req.OnEvent(mapped) } }()`). After `run.Wait(ctx)` returns, the select at line 385 waits up to **1 second** for the events channel; on timeout it proceeds WITHOUT the event goroutine having finished. So `req.OnEvent` (the execute.go checkpoint closure that mutates `task.Runtime`, `state.UpdatedAt`, and calls `SaveExecuteRunState`) can still be running concurrently AFTER `startSprintRuntime` returns.

In execute.go:
- Line 269: `run, runErr := s.startSprintRuntime(...)`
- Line 270-272: reads sessionSaveErr under sessionMu. Good.
- Line 275: `task.Runtime = mergeRuntimeSummary(...)` — NOT under sessionMu. Concurrent write with OnEvent's `task.Runtime = &ExecuteRuntimeSummary{...}` → **data race on task.Runtime**.
- Lines 283-284: `task.UpdatedAt = finish; task.CompletedAt = &finish` — concurrent writes with OnEvent's `task.UpdatedAt = s.now().UTC()`.
- Line 314: `SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state)` — concurrent save with OnEvent's save → two concurrent `saveExecuteRunStateWithHooks` writing different temp files, both renaming to same path — last-writer-wins. If OnEvent's save lands AFTER the terminal save, the persisted file could contain the PRE-terminal snapshot (running status + session checkpoint) overwriting the terminal outcome! Actually wait — OnEvent saves a snapshot where status is still "running"... no wait: the OnEvent handler sets task.Runtime but not status; at the time of the event, status was already persisted as running (line 216). So the in-memory state at event time has status=running. The main loop then sets terminal status in memory and saves. If an event arrives late (within the 1s window after Wait returned), OnEvent fires with stale in-memory state?? No — OnEvent closes over `task` pointer and `state` — the SAME objects the main goroutine is mutating. So OnEvent's save serializes whatever is currently in memory — which by then includes terminal status. The danger is torn/racing field writes (Go data race, undefined values) rather than stale overwrite. Also two concurrent Save calls → both marshal concurrently while fields mutate → JSON could capture inconsistent state, e.g., status=complete with StartedAt nil etc. Validation on save might fail or produce corrupt-but-valid file.

How real is this? The 1-second grace window: after Wait returns, if the event stream hasn't closed within 1s, StartRun returns while the pump goroutine continues delivering events to OnEvent indefinitely (until channel closes). For OpenCode adapter, events come from... let me check how run.Events() behaves after process exit — probably closes quickly. But there's no guarantee; the code explicitly tolerates 1s timeout then abandons the pump. Meanwhile the sprint loop immediately proceeds to mutate task/state and save. This is a genuine race window, though narrow in practice.

More importantly: **the checkpoint save error handling**: sessionSaveErr read at line 270-272 happens right after startSprintRuntime returns; late events arriving after that check would update sessionSaveErr but it's never re-read (checkpointErr already captured). Minor.

Severity: concurrency defect with observable bad outcome (data race → possible corrupted .run-state.json, Go race detector would flag). Trigger: slow event-stream close after turn completion (>1s). Confidence: medium-high — need to verify Events() can outlive Wait. The design (select with time.After(1s)) explicitly acknowledges the pump may not have finished. So yes — OnEvent may fire after StartRun returns. And execute.go's OnEvent writes shared state without synchronization vs main goroutine. REAL finding.

Wait, actually let me double-check: does `run.Wait()` returning guarantee Events() closed? In agentwrap, typically Wait waits for process exit; events drain asynchronously. The 1s fallback exists precisely because they can't guarantee it. Confirmed plausible.

Also note: even without the 1s timeout — between `<-waitCh` receiving and `<-eventsCh` receiving, events are being delivered concurrently while mapResult runs; but execute.go only touches state after StartRun returns. With eventsCh received, pump done → safe. The unsafe case is ONLY the 1s-timeout path. Narrow but real.

Hmm, wait — also consider ctx cancellation path: `case <-ctx.Done(): run.Cancel; select { waited or 5s timeout }`. On the 5s-timeout branch, StartRun returns mapped cancelled result while BOTH the wait goroutine and event pump are still alive. The event pump keeps calling OnEvent → keeps saving state (with running status) WHILE execute.go classifies the task as cancelled, persists terminal, breaks loop, WriteExecuteSummary, returns... and the pump can keep firing for as long as the underlying runtime streams. Each OnEvent save writes state including whatever's in memory — after terminal persist, in-memory has terminal statuses so saves stay terminal-consistent-ish, but concurrent marshaling races remain. AND: after Execute returns, the CLI calls finishDurableCLICommand etc.; the pump goroutine leaks until events close. If the runtime store DB was deleted by deleteCompletedSessions... not called on failure paths. OK.

So Finding 1: **unsynchronized OnEvent checkpointing races with post-turn state mutation and terminal persistence when the event pump outlives StartRun (1s/5s abandon windows)** — data race on ExecuteTaskRecord fields and concurrent .run-state.json writers. Evidence: runtime.go:358-401 (abandon windows), execute.go:253-268 (OnEvent mutation), execute.go:270-316 (unguarded mutations + saves). Severity: medium-high reliability (corrupt/duplicated persistence), confidence high on mechanism, trigger requires slow event close/cancellation.

Actually hold on, let me reconsider the cancellation path more carefully because it widens the window massively:

```
case <-ctx.Done():
    _ = run.Cancel(context.Background())
    select {
    case waited := <-waitCh: ...
    case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
        return mapped, ctx.Err()   // <-- returns while pump+wait goroutines STILL RUNNING
    }
```

On the 5s branch, StartRun returns to startSprintRuntime → recordRuntimeMetric → execute.go continues: classification (ctx.Err() != nil → cancelled), terminal save, break, summary write, return error. Meanwhile the abandoned `run.Wait(ctx)` goroutine eventually finishes and its result is DROPPED (sent to buffered chan). The pump keeps calling OnEvent per event. OnEvent does full `SaveExecuteRunState` per new SessionID (only first time per distinct ID — subsequent events with same ID skip). So limited number of extra saves. But each save races with main-goroutine writes. Also recordRuntimeMetric loads/writes metrics file — unrelated file.

And crucially, on this abandoned path, `retainRuntimeStore(req.RuntimeStorePath, req.RuntimeStoreOwner, ctx.Err())` was called inside the timeout branch BEFORE return — marks store retained. Fine.

So the race is real but bounded. Data-race severity in Go: undefined behavior technically; practically torn writes on string/interface fields → corrupted JSON unlikely but possible; duplicate concurrent file writes via rename are atomic per-write, so file ends up one-or-the-other, both plausibly valid JSON. The worse variant: OnEvent save happens BETWEEN line 216 (persisted running) and line 314 (terminal) — no, OnEvent during normal operation is fine because main goroutine isn't saving then. The overlap is only after StartRun returns. At that point main goroutine mutates task fields THEN saves. Overlapping OnEvent save could interleave: main sets CompletedAt, OnEvent marshals mid-mutation → JSON with status=running (old) + completedAt set? Validation requires terminal→CompletedAt non-nil; running requires StartedAt non-nil — mixed states mostly still validate. Corrupted output risk low but nonzero. The primary defect = data race (undefined behavior) + unsynchronized shared mutation. I'll report it with honest framing: narrow trigger, real race, medium severity, medium-high confidence (mechanism certain from code; practical frequency uncertain).

**Finding candidate R2 — `deleteCompletedSessions` uses `ctx` after durable cancel?** Called at line 338-340 with ctx possibly cancelled? Only when no failed tasks; ctx could be cancelled right after last success → deleteCompletedSessions with cancelled ctx → DeleteSession fails silently (`_ =`). Sessions leak until cleanup prunes. Best-effort anyway. Non-issue.

**Candidate R3 — result.SessionIDs / events.seenSessions**: On resume, batchSessionID from previous PROCESS — the OpenCode adapter must find that session. agentwrapopencode.MetadataDatabasePath points to the sprint-scoped runtime store; sessions persist there across processes (SQLite?). CleanupRuntimeStores(sp.Path, 72h...) deletes OLD stores >72h — scoped to sp.Path. Store owner includes task ID → per-task stores! ScopedRuntimeStorePath(sprintDir, owner) where owner includes ":<stage>:<task-id>". So EACH TASK gets its OWN runtime store DB. Cross-task continuation (SessionAction=continue with SessionID recorded from a DIFFERENT task's store)... does the opencode adapter resolve sessions globally or per-store? If per-store, continuing task 2's session ID from task 1's store would FAIL unless the adapter looks up by session id across... hmm. Let me check opencode.go / store.go to see whether session continuation crosses store boundaries. This is exactly context-pack unknown #2. If the adapter resolves the session only within the CURRENT request's RuntimeStorePath (task-scoped), then cross-task "continue" would fail at runtime → every multi-task run's second task errors?! But efficiency_improvements_test asserts two requests with continue action succeed using a FAKE runtime. Production adapter behavior unknown. Let me look at opencode.go and store.go.

Let me also check ScopedRuntimeStorePath.

But ALSO consider: task 1 succeeds, task 2 fails with session-not-found. Operator re-runs WITHOUT --resume → fresh state → task 1 RE-RUNS from scratch (documented retry semantics) → hits the same wall at task 2 forever. With --resume → reconcile → task 1 complete skipped, task 2 pending → batchSessionID = reusableExecuteSession(...) picks task-1's record session (model matches) → SAME broken continuation → fails identically. So the sprint is UNCOMPLETABLE via the documented flows whenever it has ≥2 tasks. Unless operator edits plan to single task or models differ per task (annotation) making continueSession false!

Escape hatch: if task 2 has a different model annotation than task 1's recorded model, continueSession=false → full prompt without session → works. So workaround exists but the default path is broken.

Severity: critical/high for the governed-sprint-delivery domain — core documented behavior ("later tasks are compact continuations") fails deterministically for any plan with multiple same-model tasks. Confidence: high (mechanism empirically verified with real opencode 1.18.23; wiring traced end-to-end). Yes runtime.go:576-582. And processSpec sets OPENCODE_DB. Confirmed end-to-end.

	req := s.runtimeConfig
	req.Prompt = prompt
	req.WorkDir = s.root
	req.Metadata = cloneMetadata(req.Metadata, metadata)
	stage := strings.TrimSpace(metadata["stage"])
	promptKind := stage
	if stage == string(VerificationPhaseQA) {
		promptKind += ".investigator"
		if role := strings.TrimSpace(metadata["role"]); role != "" {
			promptKind = stage + "." + role
		}
	}
	project := strings.TrimSpace(metadata["project"])
	sprint := strings.TrimSpace(metadata["sprint"])
	storeOwner := strings.Join([]string{"sprint", project, sprint, stage, strings.TrimSpace(metadata["task"]), strings.TrimSpace(metadata["coverage"]), strings.TrimSpace(metadata["area"])}, ":")
	req.RuntimeStoreOwner = storeOwner
	req.RuntimeStorePath = pruntime.ScopedRuntimeStorePath(filepath.Join(s.root, "projects", project, "sprints", sprint), storeOwner)
	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(prompt))
	checksum := hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])

reasoning_details.text:
Confirmed: default executable is `opencode` (the same binary I tested). Wiring is airtight:

1. execute.go:241-245 — per-task metadata `task: task.ID`; `runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path`.
2. service.go:1137-1139 — storeOwner includes task ID → distinct RuntimeStorePath per task.
3. runtime.go (ultraplan) 576-581 — metadata[MetadataDatabasePath] = req.RuntimeStorePath.
4. agentwrap opencode processSpec — OPENCODE_DB=<per-task db>.
5. Task 2 continuation: --session S1 + OPENCODE_DB(task2 fresh) → "Session not found" (empirically verified with opencode 1.18.23).
6. ultraplan opencode.go:133-138 missingSessionPolicy → PolicyDecisionStop → no retry/fallback.
7. Classification: runtime-failed → task failed → break → "execute completed with failed tasks" → ExitPartial.

This is Finding #1, high severity, very high confidence.

One more check for completeness: does anything in the frozen repo pin an OLDER opencode version where OPENCODE_DB didn't isolate sessions? Not checkable; but the current default binary exhibits it. Also note the same commit introduced DeleteRuntimeStore preference in deleteCompletedSessions — consistent with intent to isolate. The sprint flow just wasn't updated.

Also note interplay with `deleteCompletedSessions`: after ALL tasks resolve... unreachable for multi-task anyway.

Additional related sub-defect worth folding in or listing separately: **cross-process `--resume` reuse across DIFFERENT tasks** has the same problem (resume queue continues at task N+1 with session from task N's store — different owner → not found). Same root cause.

Now let me continue with other candidates and examine tests + remaining paths. Next:
1. Read efficiency_improvements_test.go to confirm fake-runtime coverage (evidence for why this slipped through).
2. Examine durable_operations.go for resume wiring & cancellation.
3. Check verify.go ExecuteComplete.
4. Look at operation_runner.go web path.

162: 	if owned == nil {
163: 		return false, runcontrol.ErrNotFound
164: 	}
165: 	owned.eventMu.Lock()
166: 	defer owned.eventMu.Unlock()

169: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventWarning
170: 	}

177: 		}
178: 		owned.omitted++

194: 		}
195: 	}

197: 	if event.Message != "" {

199: 	}

201: 		if omission == nil {
202: 			omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced"}

206: 		owned.omitted = 0

210: 		Kind: event.EventKind, Tool: event.Tool, Action: event.Action, Reason: event.Reason,

212: 	})

223: func (m *durableOperationManager) controlOperation(ctx context.Context, owned *ownedDurableOperation) {
224: 	defer close(owned.done)
225: 	ticker := time.NewTicker(runcontrol.OwnerTickInterval)
226: 	defer ticker.Stop()
227: 	lastHeartbeat, lastReconcile := time.Now(), time.Now()
228: 	for {
229: 		select {
230: 		case <-ctx.Done():

232: 		case <-owned.stop:
233: 			return
234: 		case now := <-ticker.C:
235: 			snapshot, err := m.repository.Snapshot(ctx, owned.fence.RunID)
236: 			if err != nil {

238: 				return
239: 			}
240: 			if snapshot.Cancellation.State == runcontrol.CancellationRequested {
241: 				if _, _, err := m.repository.AcknowledgeCancellation(ctx, owned.fence); err != nil {
242: 					owned.cancel()
243: 					return
244: 				}
245: 				owned.cancel()
246: 				return
247: 			}
248: 			if now.Sub(lastHeartbeat) >= runcontrol.HeartbeatInterval {

250: 					owned.cancel()
251: 					return
252: 				}
253: 				lastHeartbeat = now
254: 			}
255: 			if now.Sub(lastReconcile) >= runcontrol.ReconciliationInterval {

257: 					owned.cancel()
258: 					return
259: 				}

261: 			}
262: 		}
263: 	}
264: }

269: 	delete(m.owned, runID)
270: 	m.mu.Unlock()
271: 	if owned == nil {

273: 	}
274: 	owned.eventMu.Lock()
275: 	if owned.omitted > 0 {
276: 		_, _, appendErr := appendRunEventWithRetry(ctx, m.repository, owned.fence, runcontrol.EventDraft{Type: runcontrol.EventOmission, Omission: &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced", Count: owned.omitted, FirstAt: &owned.omittedFirst, LastAt: &owned.omittedLast}})
277: 		if appendErr != nil && runErr == nil {
278: 			runErr = appendErr
279: 		}
280: 		owned.omitted = 0
281: 	}
282: 	owned.eventMu.Unlock()
283: 	close(owned.stop)
284: 	<-owned.done
285: 	owned.cancel()
286: 	outcome := runcontrol.TerminalSucceeded
287: 	reason := "operation completed"
288: 	switch {
289: 	case errors.Is(runErr, context.DeadlineExceeded):
290: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalTimedOut, "operation deadline exceeded"
291: 	case errors.Is(runErr, context.Canceled), state == OperationCancelled:
292: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalCancelled, "operation cancelled"
293: 	case runErr != nil, state == OperationFailed:
294: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalFailed, "operation failed"
295: 	case state == OperationPartial:
296: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalInterrupted, "operation interrupted"
297: 	}
298: 	_, _, err := proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(ctx, m.repository, owned.fence, runcontrol.TerminalProposal{Outcome: outcome, Reason: reason, ProposedBy: m.owner.ID})
299: 	return err
300: }
